title: Ferret
text:
# Ferret

The ferret (Mustela furo) is a small, domesticated species of the family Mustelidae. It descends
from the European polecat and was domesticated at least 2,500 years ago, probably to hunt rabbits.

Ferrets sleep 14 to 18 hours a day and are most active around dawn and dusk. They are curious and
known for stealing and hoarding small objects. The name fits: it comes from the Latin
furitto, "little thief". A group of ferrets is called a business.
